provider.name: process_pisco_profiles
provider.description: Post-processing of PIScO profiles: EcoTaxa export and upload.

tools.name: pisco_ecotaxa_export
tools.description: Export an EcoTaxa import archive from the C++ segmenter's result.h5. Writes one PNG per object plus an ecotaxa_<profile>.tsv with acquisition metadata and zooprocess morphometrics, zipped ready for import. If pisco_deconvolve ran before extraction the crops are already deconvolved. Also writes particles_<profile>.h5, the complete measured object table (no images) that abundances are computed from.

sourcePath.description: Segmenter results directory holding result.h5, or the result.h5 itself. This is the OBJECT_EXTRACTION output, not the correction checkpoints.

targetPath.description: Directory for the crops, the TSV and the zip. Leave empty to let the Hub choose.

profileName.description: Profile name, used as EcoTaxa sample_id and in the archive filename. Empty uses the results directory name.

maxZipSizeMb.description: Split the export into multiple archives above this size. Each part carries its own TSV.

minSize.description: Drop objects whose bounding box width and height are both at or below this many pixels. 0 keeps everything the segmenter found.

gaugePressure.description: Treat the pressure in the frame name as gauge pressure. By default it is absolute and 10.1325 dbar is subtracted to give depth.

ctdCast.description: Running number of the CTD cast PIScO rode on; written to every object as sample_ctd_cast. Optional.

linkBase.description: Hub base URL, e.g. http://10.11.11.110:5000. When set, every object gets an EcoTaxa object_link that opens the HDF profile viewer on that object in its frame. Leave empty for no links.

scaleBar.description: Draw a scale bar under each crop. Uses the repo's reversible strip: the crop's own pixels are untouched and its original size is recorded in the PNG, so strip_scale_bar() restores it exactly before the crop reaches a classifier. The bar is 1 mm where it fits and 500 um otherwise.

pixelSizeUm.description: Micrometres per pixel, for the scale bar and object_esd alike. 22.5 is PISCO2; set the camera's own value for any other.

predictionsPath.description: pisco_vit_classify output directory (or its predictions.csv). Its labels are written into the TSV as annotations, so predictions arrive with the import and no second trip to EcoTaxa is needed. In a dual-ViT chain point this at the LAST stage: with carryForward on it already covers every object, the taxon labels where it classified and the binary verdict elsewhere. Comma-separating several stages also works for manual runs, applied in order. Chain with {"$from": {"task": N, "output": "predictions"}}.

taxonomyMapPath.description: ecotaxa_taxonomy_map.json. Required when predictionsPath is set: the TSV carries numeric EcoTaxa taxon ids (object_annotation_category_id), not label names, because names are ambiguous. Export fails if the map still has unresolved labels.

isolateCrops.description: Write each crop as the object alone in a tight box, everything outside its mask white - the crop the python route saved and the classifier was trained on. Off writes the segmenter's stored box as-is, with its padding and any neighbours.

subsampleMax.description: Export at most this many not-living objects, drawn at random but reproducibly (the same ones on a re-export); every living object is exported regardless. 0 exports all. Needs predictionsPath. The kept fraction is written to subsample.json beside the export, for scaling not-living abundances back up.

notLivingLabel.description: Label of the binary stage's not-living class, resolved through the taxonomy map. Only used with subsampleMax.

particleTable.description: Also write particles_<profile>.h5 beside the export: every object, measured like the TSV, with its prediction and whether it went to EcoTaxa, but no images. Abundances are computed from it, since the archive may hold only a subsample of the not-living objects.

outputs.name: export
outputs.description: EcoTaxa import archive(s), crops and TSV, and the particle table

tools.name: pisco_vit_classify
tools.description: Run a ViT over the crops in the segmenter's result.h5. One stage of the dual-ViT setup: chain two tasks, a binary living/not-living pass over everything (with emitEmbeddings on), then a taxon pass restricted to the living ones. Reads crops straight from the HDF5, so no scale bar to strip and isolation stays a choice made at inference time.

sourcePath.description: Segmenter results directory holding result.h5, or the file itself.

targetPath.description: Directory for predictions.csv and, if requested, embeddings.npz. Leave empty to let the Hub choose.

modelPath.description: Model directory on this machine, or a Hugging Face repo id (e.g. Veit/diplo-vit-plankton). This is the stage's model: the binary one for the first pass, the taxon one for the second. A pisco_vit_train output directory also works - its best_model/ is found automatically - so a retrained model can be chained straight in with {"$from": {"task": N, "output": "model"}}.

isolateCrops.description: Cut each crop to its mask's box and white out everything outside the mask - the crop the python route saved and the ViTs were trained on. Off feeds the segmenter's stored box as-is, with its padding and any neighbours in it.

emitEmbeddings.description: Also write the encoder CLS vectors, for EcoTaxa's similarity search. Set this on the stage that sees EVERY object (the binary one): EcoTaxa disables similarity search for a whole project if any object lacks a feature vector.

batchSize.description: Crops per GPU batch. 64 fits an 8 GB card in fp32; 256 is fine on a 3080 in fp16.

topK.description: How many ranked labels to record per object.

restrictToPath.description: Earlier stage's output directory (or its predictions.csv). Only objects whose top1 label is in restrictLabels are classified. This is how the taxon stage is limited to living crops; chain it with {"$from": {"task": 0, "output": "predictions"}}.

restrictLabels.description: Comma-separated top1 labels to keep, when restrictToPath is set.

carryForward.description: With restrictToPath, keep the earlier stage's rows for objects this stage skips, so predictions.csv covers every object. Leave on: it lets a downstream task reference this stage alone, which matters because the Hub resolves $from inside dicts but not inside lists, so two references cannot be combined in one setting.

workers.description: Processes preprocessing crops while the GPU runs the previous batch. Leave unset for up to 8 (one less than the cores); 0 does it inline.

precision.description: auto runs fp16 on GPUs with tensor cores (RTX 3060/3080) and fp32 on Pascal (Tesla P4), where fp16 is slower.

tools.name: pisco_ecotaxa_features
tools.description: Push ViT embeddings into EcoTaxa so its "similar to" filter works. Reduces them to the vector(50) the schema requires and writes obj_cnn_features_vector directly - there is no REST endpoint for features. Runs on the machine that owns the EcoTaxa database, so Postgres can stay on loopback.

embeddingsPath.description: embeddings.npz from pisco_vit_classify, or that stage's output directory. Must come from the stage that saw EVERY object.

projectId.description: EcoTaxa project to attach the features to. Leave unset and use projectIdFrom to chain off an import task. Its objects' orig_id must equal the object_id in the embeddings.

pcaPath.description: PCA basis .npz. Fitted and written on first use, loaded and reused afterwards. Keep one basis per encoder: projects reduced under different bases are not comparable, and the table has no field to tell them apart.

dsn.description: Postgres connection string. Empty uses the local EcoTaxa stack on loopback.

allowPartial.description: Write even when some objects would have no vector. EcoTaxa refuses to run a similarity search on such a project, so this is for debugging only.

projectIdFrom.description: pisco_ecotaxa_import output directory (or its import.json). Attaches features to the project that step created, so the whole chain runs without a human carrying the project number across. Use instead of projectId.

tools.name: pisco_ecotaxa_import
tools.description: Import an exported archive into EcoTaxa. Creates a new project by default, or adds to an existing one when projectId is set. For an EcoTaxa that shares a filesystem with the Hub nothing is copied - the share is mounted inside its server load area, so the archive is imported where it already sits. For a remote instance such as ecotaxa.obs-vlfr.fr, set uploadArchive and it goes to EcoTaxa's FTP drop first. Writes import.json with the project id, so a following task can attach features to the project this one created.

archivePath.description: The .zip to import, or the export task's output directory. A split export (several zips) all goes into the same project. Chain with {"$from": {"task": N, "output": "export"}}.

targetPath.description: Directory for import.json, which records the project id. Leave empty to let the Hub choose.

projectId.description: Import into this existing project. Leave unset to create a new one.

projectTitle.description: Title for the new project. Empty uses the archive's name. Ignored when projectId is set.

instrument.description: Instrument for a new project. Must be one EcoTaxa knows - there is no PIScO entry, so 'Other camera' is the generic that works.

visible.description: Whether a newly created project is visible to all users.

access.description: Who may use the project. 'public' lets every user view; 'open' also lets them annotate and change settings through the API, but EcoTaxa's GUI ignores it and still shows view-only, so for annotation by everyone grant it with ecotaxa_grant_annotators.py instead; 'private' only those granted. Empty follows 'visible'. Applied to an existing project too when projectId is set.

updateMode.description: Empty imports as new. 'Yes' updates existing data, 'Cla' also updates classifications. Use with skipExistingObjects to re-import without duplicating.

skipExistingObjects.description: Skip objects already present, rather than adding them again.

url.description: EcoTaxa base URL, WITHOUT a trailing /api (the tool appends it). Empty uses the local instance on loopback; for the public instance use https://ecotaxa.obs-vlfr.fr together with uploadArchive.

uploadArchive.description: Drop each archive on EcoTaxa's FTP and import it from there. Required for any instance that does not share a filesystem with the Hub, such as ecotaxa.obs-vlfr.fr; needs an "ftp" block in the credentials file. Leave off for a co-located instance, where the archive is imported where it already sits.

credentialsPath.description: JSON file holding {"user": ..., "password": ...} for this instance. Empty uses /opt/pisco/etc/ecotaxa.json. Credentials stay in a file on the machine because task settings are rendered to disk in plain text.

tools.name: pisco_ecotaxa_labels
tools.description: Fetch validated labels out of an EcoTaxa project, as the starting point for retraining the dual ViT. Writes labels.csv: one row per validated object, giving the crop's identity and the taxon a human confirmed. Only validated objects are taken - predicted ones carry this pipeline's own output, and training on those would teach the model its own mistakes. Runs on the EcoTaxa machine because credentials live there rather than in task settings.

projectIds.description: EcoTaxa project ids, comma-separated, in priority order. The LAST project wins on a duplicate crop: EcoTaxa subsets are copies, so the same crop appears in a project and in every subset drawn from it, and letting the later one win means a re-validation supersedes the original call.

targetPath.description: Directory for labels.csv and labels.json. Leave empty to let the Hub choose.

statusFilter.description: EcoTaxa status to fetch: V validated, P predicted, D dubious, empty for all. Leave at V for training - anything else feeds the model its own predictions back.

url.description: EcoTaxa base URL. Empty uses the local instance on loopback.

outputs.name: labels
outputs.description: labels.csv, plus labels.json with the class histogram

tools.name: pisco_vit_trainset
tools.description: Assemble a dual-ViT training set from validated labels and the run those objects came from. Writes two imagefolders - binary/ (living vs not-living) and multiclass/ (the living taxa) - ready for pisco_vit_train. Crops are read from the segmenter's result.h5 through the same code path inference uses, so the training crops are the crops the classifier will see; the old python pipeline's deconv_crops zips are also accepted, which is how already-validated pre-Hub projects can still be trained from. EcoTaxa export zips are deliberately not a source: their PNGs carry a scale bar.

labelsPath.description: labels.csv from pisco_ecotaxa_labels, or that task's output directory. Chain with {"$from": {"task": N, "output": "labels"}}.

cropsPath.description: Comma-separated roots holding the images these labels describe: segmenter results directories (searched for result.h5) and/or old-pipeline output holding deconv_crops*.zip. Point this at the run the EcoTaxa objects were exported from.

targetPath.description: Directory for binary/, multiclass/ and trainset.json. Leave empty to let the Hub choose.

isolateCrops.description: Mask neighbouring objects out to white when reading from HDF5. This is one of the axes a classifier is bound to: set it to the isolateCrops the trained model will be RUN with in pisco_vit_classify. Getting it wrong is an out-of-domain shift, not a cosmetic difference.

nonLiving.description: Comma-separated classes forming the binary not-living side; everything else counts as living. bubble and t001 belong here when present - they are imaging artifacts, and calling them living reintroduces the false positives the not-living screening removes.

excludeMulticlass.description: Comma-separated living classes to leave out of the multiclass set, e.g. 'multiple species': fused objects are a segmentation problem, not something to ask the classifier to name.

minPerClass.description: Drop a multiclass class with fewer crops than this. Below it a class cannot be split into train/validation/test, and its reported F1 says nothing about model quality.

outputs.name: trainset
outputs.description: binary/ and multiclass/ imagefolders, plus trainset.json recording how the set was built

tools.name: pisco_vit_train
tools.description: Fine-tune one stage of the dual ViT on a training set from pisco_vit_trainset. Run it twice against the same trainset - stage=binary and stage=multiclass - because the two stages start from different checkpoints and answer different questions. Writes best_model/, which pisco_vit_classify can be pointed straight at, plus eval_report.json with per-class precision/recall and the confusion matrix. Preprocessing is asserted at startup to match the inference path exactly, so the trained model and the classifier cannot drift apart.

dataPath.description: pisco_vit_trainset output directory, or an imagefolder directly. Chain with {"$from": {"task": N, "output": "trainset"}}.

stage.description: Which half of the trainset to train: 'binary' or 'multiclass'. Leave empty when dataPath already points at an imagefolder.

initModel.description: Checkpoint to fine-tune: a model directory on this machine, or a Hugging Face repo id. Use the previous model for this stage - its head is reinitialised automatically when the class set differs. Training from google/vit-base-patch16-224-in21k instead wants a learningRate of roughly 2e-4.

targetPath.description: Directory for best_model/, eval_report.json and labels.json. Leave empty to let the Hub choose.

epochs.description: Passes over the training split. The checkpoint kept is the one with the best validation accuracy, not the last.

learningRate.description: AdamW learning rate, decayed linearly to zero with no warmup. 5e-5 suits fine-tuning an existing model.

seed.description: Seeds the stratified 70/15/15 split and the training run, so a rerun on the same trainset is reproducible.

workers.description: Dataloader worker processes decoding and augmenting crops.

precision.description: auto uses fp16 only where the GPU has tensor cores (compute capability 7.0+). On Pascal cards such as the Tesla P4 fp16 is slower than fp32, so auto correctly stays in fp32 there.

outputs.name: model
outputs.description: best_model/ (point pisco_vit_classify's modelPath at it), eval_report.json, labels.json
